subject: b95J01:B6-B7 — how normality turns k into a divisor of the index

nodes.claim: How does normality of H give that k divides the index [G:H], given that the criterion of part (a) only speaks about integers m with g^m in H?

With H normal the cosets form the quotient group G/H of order [G:H]; the coset gH has order k by part (a), and Lagrange makes the order of an element divide the order of the group. Concretely g^[G:H] is in H, and applying the membership criterion to m = [G:H] gives k | [G:H].
H is normal in G, so the set of left cosets carries a group structure.
The order of the coset gH in G/H is the least positive j with g^j in H, which is k by part (a).
g raised to the index lies in H, the form the Lean proof uses.
In a finite group, Lagrange's theorem makes the order of an element divide the order of the group; applied to gH in G/H, k divides [G:H].
k divides [G:H], and the membership criterion at m = [G:H] is the explicit route.
